1-800-GOT-JUNK for Fence Removal Debris

Got an old fence that’s finally coming down? Whether you’re renovating your backyard, upgrading to a new design, or simply clearing space, the leftover wood, metal posts, concrete footings, and fasteners can feel like a mountain of junk. That’s where 1-800-GOT-JUNK? steps in. In this guide we’ll walk through why professional fence debris removal matters, how the 1-800‑GOT‑JUNK? process works, and what you can do to keep the experience smooth and budget‑friendly.

Why Choose Professional Fence Debris Removal?

It might be tempting to tackle the clean‑up yourself—after all, a shovel and a truck sound simple enough. But professional junk removal offers three big advantages:

  • Safety first: Heavy fence posts, sharp metal brackets, and concrete chunks can cause injuries if handled incorrectly.
  • Time savings: A crew can clear a full fence in a fraction of the time it would take a DIYer, freeing you to focus on the next phase of your project.
  • Environmental responsibility: 1-800‑GOT‑JUNK? partners with local recycling facilities to divert wood, metal, and concrete from landfills whenever possible.

When you call 1-800-GOT-JUNK?, you’re not just getting a truck; you’re getting a trained team that knows how to lift, load, and sort debris safely and efficiently.

How 1-800-GOT-JUNK? Handles Fence Debris

1. Quick Online Scheduling

Start by visiting the 1-800‑GOT‑JUNK? website or giving them a call. The scheduling tool lets you pick a date and time that fits your calendar. A friendly representative will confirm the details and answer any quick questions you have about the job.

2. On‑Site Assessment (Optional)

For larger jobs, the crew may perform a brief walk‑through to gauge volume and identify any special items (e.g., treated wood that requires separate disposal). This step helps avoid surprise fees.

3. Loading Day

When the crew arrives, they’ll bring all the necessary equipment—hand trucks, straps, and safety gear. They’ll load the fence sections, posts, concrete footings, and any associated hardware into their truck, taking care to keep wood separate from metal for optimal recycling.

4. Sorting and Recycling

After collection, the debris is taken to a regional facility where wood is chipped for mulch, metal is melted down, and concrete is crushed for use in road base. 1-800-GOT-JUNK? provides a recycling report upon request, so you can see exactly how much material was diverted from the landfill.

Step‑by‑Step: What to Expect on the Day of Removal

  • Arrival: The crew typically arrives within the scheduled window (often a two‑hour slot).
  • Safety briefing: They’ll explain any site restrictions—like driveway access or pet zones.
  • Loading: With proper lifting techniques, they’ll load all debris. You don’t need to be present, but many homeowners like to watch the process to ensure nothing is missed.
  • Payment: After the job, you’ll receive an itemized invoice. Most locations accept cash, major credit cards, or electronic payment.

Because the service is “all‑in‑one,” there’s no need for you to rent a dumpster, drive a truck to a landfill, or worry about local disposal ordinances.

Cost Factors & Pricing Transparency

Pricing for fence removal debris varies based on three main factors:

  1. Volume: The more cubic feet of material, the higher the charge. 1-800‑GOT‑JUNK? uses a simple volume‑based pricing model that’s easy to understand.
  2. Material type: Treated wood or hazardous components may incur a small additional fee for proper handling.
  3. Location: Urban areas or places with limited access may have a modest mileage surcharge.

The good news? 1-800-GOT-JUNK? offers a “no‑hidden‑fees” guarantee. The estimate you receive before the crew arrives is the amount you’ll pay—unless you add extra items after the fact.

Tips for Preparing Your Site

Even though the crew handles the heavy lifting, a few simple prep steps can keep the process seamless:

  • Clear the pathway: Move any garden tools, toys, or pets out of the way of the loading zone.
  • Separate hazardous items: If you have any asbestos‑containing insulation or lead‑painted metal, set those aside and let the crew know.
  • Mark boundaries: If your fence runs along a shared property line, flag where the removal ends to avoid disputes with neighbors.

These quick actions reduce the time the crew spends navigating obstacles, which can help keep your project on budget.

Eco‑Friendly Disposal Practices

Environmental stewardship is a core value for 1-800-GOT-JUNK?. Here’s how they keep your fence debris green:

  1. Wood recycling: Untreated timber is chipped and sold as mulch or animal bedding.
  2. Metal recovery: Steel and iron posts are melted and reused in new construction.
  3. Concrete repurposing: Crushed concrete becomes road base or landscaping fill.

By choosing a professional service, you’re ensuring that the maximum amount of material is recovered, which reduces the carbon footprint of your project.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Can 1-800-GOT-JUNK? remove concrete footings?

Yes. Concrete footings are heavy, but the crew is equipped with pallet jacks and loading ramps to safely lift and transport them to the recycling facility.
